display.title: Shabbos Candles: Asher Kiddeshanu, How Fortunate We Are
display.summary_short: The next words of the Shabbos candle brachah, 'Asher Kiddeshanu': a mitzvah makes us holy, and the Alter Rebbe teaches that 'asher' also means how fortunate we are.
display.summary_long: A short Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, part of a series on the brachah over Shabbos candles. Uncle Yossi teaches the next two words of the brachah, 'Asher Kiddeshanu', 'Who has made us holy'. When we make a brachah we thank Hashem, the King of the world, for the honor and privilege of doing a mitzvah, and doing it makes us holy, a holy nation close to Hashem. He then shares 'a secret' from the Alter Rebbe: besides its plain meaning, the word 'asher' is related to 'ashrei', fortunate. So 'Asher Kiddeshanu' also means how lucky and fortunate we are to be able to do a mitzvah and become holier and closer to Hashem.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah makes us holy, and we should feel how fortunate we are to be able to do it.

date.note: Aired in episode 258, during Chanukah 5747 (Friday candle time given for January 2).
